name: Point Nepean Heritage Walk
address: Point Nepean National Park, Portsea VIC 3944
signature: Walk through Fort Nepean's WWI and WWII fortifications to the very tip of the Peninsula — ocean on one side, bay on the other
editorNote:
The Point Nepean Heritage Walk is the full 8km return journey from the visitor centre to Fort Nepean at the tip of the Peninsula — through 140 years of military history, past gun emplacements and underground tunnels, to the point where Port Phillip Bay meets Bass Strait in a tidal rush through the Heads.

Fort Nepean fired the first Allied shot of both World War I (1914) and World War II (1939). The fortifications are substantial and well-interpreted, and the dual-ocean view from the tip — bay on the left, Bass Strait on the right, ships threading through the Heads — is one of the most memorable landscapes on the entire Peninsula.

Book an entry pass online (Parks Victoria). A Portsea Bus operates between the visitor centre and the fort on weekends and school holidays for those who want to reduce walking. Bikes permitted. Allow 4–5 hours for the full walk. Bring water.
whyWeGo: History, military ruins, and standing at the literal end of the Peninsula where two bodies of water meet.
ifOnlyOneThing: Walk all the way to the tip. The tidal rush through the Heads — and the knowledge of where you are standing — makes the whole trip worth it.
